rules.title: California application screening fee limits
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket costs and time, capped at $30 per applicant (adjusted annually for CPI since 1998). No fee if no unit is available; the landlord must give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts, and either process applications in order or refund the fee to unselected applicants.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.effective_date_note: Document says section updated Jan. 1, 2026; original effective date of the cap not stated.
rules.conflict_note: No single official current dollar figure is published; the $30 base is CPI-adjusted annually.

parsed.doc_summary: California Civil Code § 1950.6 (mirror): caps rental application screening fees at $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted), and sets conditions on charging, receipts, and refunds.
